articles.title: Claude’s updated Fable and Mythos models watermark their replies
articles.description: Anthropic has announced the arrival of its latest Claude models, and just as it promised last month, the new models will add invisible watermarks to all their text replies. Claude Fable 5.1 is now generally available in the Claude desktop app and other platforms, while Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to Anthropic’s “trusted access program.” While both models are the same, Mythos lands with less stringent safeguards to “support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences.” In its announcement, Anthropic shows off a variety of benchmarks demonstrating the performance boosts the two models, complete with double-digit increases when it comes to agentic scientific research, agentic coding, and business workflows. Anthropic also says both Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 were evaluated using the company’s new safety and alignment procedures, developed in response to Anthropic’s disclosures of Claude models hacking outside companies during internal testing. Specifically, Mythos 5.1 is “less likely than Mythos 5 to try to access resources outside of its test environment when assigned an otherwise impossible task,” Anthropic said. Beyond their agentic capabilities and upgraded safeguards, through, Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 mark the first Claude models to watermark their text and file outputs , in accordance with the EU AI Act. “As we recently explained, this watermark is invisible to anyone who does not have the detection API,” Anthropic wrote in its announcement. “It has no practical impact on the quality or content of Claude’s outputs and contains no information about the user, their organization, or their conversations with Claude.” As for the detection API, Anthropic says is now available to regulators, law enforcement, media, fact-checkers, independent researches, and other “eligible groups” as defined by the just-enacted EU law, adding that it will “expand access to the detection API over time.” You can apply for access to the API via this signup form . Anthropic had previously stated it would add watermark support to any new Claude models released after August 2, 2026. Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the first new Claude models to arrive subsequent to that date, while older Claude models will eventually add watermarking support as well, Anthropic has previously said. Claude text watermarking works by “nudging” the model’s word choices during the inference process, meaning the model might pick one word over another in cases where there are multiple likely options. Designed to survive a copy-and-paste as well as light editing, the watermarks are invisible, but the text patterns can be pinpointed using Anthropic’s detection API. While the presence of a Claude text watermark would show that a piece of text had been either written or “processed” by Claude, the absence of a watermark doesn’t necessarily mean the text was written by a human.

articles.title: AJK govt announces phased restoration of internet services
articles.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government has announced a phased restoration of internet services across the region, with broadband and cellular data services to resume fully in some districts while access will remain restricted to educational institutions and banks in others. The Home Department, in a notification issued on Sunday, directed the secretary of the Ministry of Interior to initiate restoration of broadband and cellular data services from Monday (Aug 31) according to a district-wise schedule. Under the schedule, full broadband and cellular data services will be restored in Neelum district, including Upper and Lower Neelum, as well as Leepa Valley and Haveli district. Broadband services will also be restored throughout Bhimber and Mirpur districts. In Muzaffarabad district, broadband access will be confined to educational institutions — schools, colleges and universities — and banks. The same arrangement will apply in Jhelum Valley. In Bagh district, broadband services will be available only to educational institutions and banks within the municipal limits of Bagh and Dhirkot. Similarly, in Kotli district, broadband access will be restricted to educational institutions and banks, except in Sehnsa, Sarsawa and Tattapani where services will remain shut. No internet services will be restored in Rawalakot and Sudhnoti districts, where the suspension will continue. Bankers in the capital welcomed the restoration, saying it would ease pressure on branches that had been handling a heavy volume of customers in the absence of digital banking facilities. Ordinary citizens, however, expressed disappointment over the limited scope of the restoration, particularly those dependent on the internet for their livelihoods. Faisal Javed, president of the Association of Pharmacies and Medical Stores, said the suspension had severely disrupted electronic payments, leaving both traders and customers in difficulty. Internet services were suspended across AJK on June 5 amid a law and order situation following the government’s decision to proscribe the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

articles.title: House Klaus / Neo Architects
articles.description: The project brief called for the design of a contemporary six-bedroom coastal residence on a steeply sloping site within the Romansbaai Estate. The client's vision was to maximise panoramic sea views while creating a home that responds sensitively to the site's topography, prevailing winds and strict height restrictions. The residence was required to integrate generous indoor and outdoor living spaces, wellness facilities, guest accommodation and sustainable design strategies, including solar energy, rainwater harvesting and green roofs. The architectural response sought to balance luxury with environmental sensitivity, producing a durable, low-maintenance home that seamlessly connects with the surrounding fynbos landscape and evolving coastal context.
